memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'This is a lasting ordinance for the generations to come, wherever you live: You must not eat any fat or any blood.'" - Lev 3:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes with a permanent boundary. No fat, no blood — not just at the tabernacle, but wherever you live.

The fat was withheld because it belonged to God. The blood was withheld for a weightier reason, which Leviticus later explains: the life of a creature is in the blood, and God gave it for making atonement (Lev 17:11). Blood was too significant to treat as ordinary food. It represented life, and life belongs to God alone.

So Israel carried this restriction into every kitchen in the land. Every meal, in every home, quietly rehearsed a truth: life is sacred, and it belongs to God.

The New Testament makes clear that these food restrictions were part of the old covenant order, fulfilled and set aside in Christ. Jesus declared all foods clean (Mk 7:19), and Peter was told plainly not to call impure what God has made clean (Acts 10:15). We are not bound by this ordinance today.

But the truth underneath it is permanent. The blood still matters — because it was ultimately pointing to blood that was poured out for us. Christ redeemed us not with perishable things but with his precious blood (1 Pet 1:18-19).

Israel was never allowed to consume the blood. Jesus, astonishingly, invites us to receive His life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I treat life — mine and others' — as sacred and belonging to God?
2. What does it mean to me that Christ freely gave the very thing Israel was forbidden to touch?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You taught Israel that life is sacred and Yours alone. Thank You that Your Son poured out His life so that I could receive Yours. Amen.
